 Follow ‘Law and Order: Special Victims Unit’ Has Surprise Schedule Change on NBC After 600th Episode
 Yana Grebenyuk Thu, November 19, 2026 at 3:17 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Virginia Sherwood/NBC Law & Order: Special Victims Unit is the latest show to experience a surprise schedule change ahead of its fall finale.
 The hit NBC series will not be airing a new episode on Thursday, November 19. Instead, the network has plans to premiere the second part of The Traitors: New Blood finale in Law & Order: SVU 's time slot.
 The shakeup will continue into next week with no episode on Thursday, November 26, in favor of a Thanksgiving Day football game. This comes after Law & Order: Special Victims Unit celebrated its 600th episode.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement During the milestone moment, which aired November 12, Mariska Hargitay reunited with her former costar Christopher Meloni .
 Why Did Chris Meloni Leave 'Law and Order: SVU' Before 'Organized Crime'? Pay Dispute Explained 
 Creator Dick Wolf launched the Law & Order universe in 1990. Law & Order: Special Victims Unit premiered in 1999 as the first spinoff of the original series, with Meloni and Hargitay starring as Elliot Stabler and Olivia Benson, respectively. (Additional shows in the franchise include Law & Order: Criminal Intent, Law & Order: Trial by Jury, Law & Order: LA and Law & Order True Crime .)
 Meloni, 65, shocked SVU fans after season 12 by announcing his exit from the hit series. In real life, Meloni revealed that a pay dispute contributed to his decision. On the show, Stabler's exit was explained as a retirement move.
 Advertisement Advertisement "I left with zero animosity, but I did leave clearly and open-eyed in going forward and finding new adventures. I was like, 'That's what I want to do, keep moving forward,'" Meloni told the New York Post in July 2021. "I had done the Law & Order way of storytelling, which they do really well, and I was interested in telling stories from a different angle — whether comedic or inhabiting a new world or doing it on different platforms."
 Hargitay, 62, meanwhile, weighed in on losing her scene partner after more than a decade.
 Midseason 2027 TV Schedule: See When 'Grey's Anatomy,' 'Tracker' and More Air After Several Changes 
 "I was just so sad, because we started this thing and built it together," she told People at the time. "And we went through so many milestones and spent so much time together and understood so many things that nobody else could understand."
 Advertisement Advertisement Meloni, however, saw things differently. "She was left in the familiarity of what we were. And I'm sure there were echoes, constant reminders, everywhere. But for me, it was about how things fell out — and the word I'll use is that it was inelegant," he said.
 Meloni added: "At the end of the day, how it was handled was, 'OK, see you later.' So I went, 'That's fine. We're all big boys and girls here. See you later.' And I was off on new adventures and doing what I wanted to do. Telling the stories I wanted to tell."
 News broke nearly a decade later that Meloni would reprise his role in Law & Order: Organized Crime. The spinoff, which premiered in 2021, went through quite a few showrunner shakeups before being canceled in April after season 5.
 New episodes of Law and Order: SVU premiere on NBC Thursdays at 9 p.m. ET and are available to stream the next day on Peacock.
